- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in early forecast days when history shows recent volatility or downward trends — fails to recognize mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model continues upward trend for 2–3 days before adjusting — exhibits lag.
- Model underestimates prices when true outcome is below 65–70, especially if recent history shows low values — fails to recognize potential rebound.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term volatility spikes and overestimates long-term trends.
- When true outcome is below 60, model often fails to recognize the risk of further decline — underestimates downside risk.
- Model overestimates prices when history includes recent high values — fails to recognize potential mean reversion or correction.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when history includes recent high prices — fails to adjust for potential correction.
- Model tends to underestimate prices when true outcome is below 65 and history shows recent low values — fails to recognize potential rebound.
